_about: Which generic course each British Flat course races on until it has its own build in the game (owner, 19 Nov 2026: 'these will form a stop gap meaning we can play any course we want'). Families from the course sheet's 'Generic courses' tab; the hand from the real course. A race picks the generic course's start nearest its own distance (see 'starts'). Courses already built in full (Ascot, Newmarket's Rowley Mile and July Course, York) race on their own builds; the tier 1 and tier 2 builds (Goodwood, Epsom, Newbury, Doncaster, Chester, Sandown) are listed so they have a stand-in until their own build goes into the game.

starts.note: the right-handed courses have the same starts; a race takes the nearest start (e.g. 1m3f -> 1m4f, 1m5f -> 1m6f, 2m4f+ -> 2m on the Park, the longest); a real course's round sprints (Bath, Wetherby, Chester) can take the '6f (round)' start on the Tight Track if moved there

Bath.why: left-handed, steady climb to the post, sprints on the turn

Carlisle.why: right-handed pear, against the collar over the last 4f

Catterick.why: small sharp left-handed oval with a sprint spur

Chepstow.why: left-handed oval with a straight mile (undulating)

Chester.why: tight, near-circular, left-handed (own build in progress)

Doncaster.why: galloping, straight mile, round-mile chute (own build in progress)

Epsom.why: left-handed, downhill turn into a cambered run-in (own build)

Ffos Las.why: flat left-handed oval with a straight 6f

Goodwood.why: right-handed, undulating, downhill sprint course (own build)

Haydock.why: galloping left-handed oval with a 6f straight (tier 2, to build)

Lingfield (AW).why: small sharp left-handed all-weather loop, short run-in

Lingfield (turf).why: left-handed triangle, a climb then a downhill turn in, a straight 7f

Musselburgh.why: small right-handed oval with a 5f straight

Newbury.why: galloping, straight mile (own build in progress)

Newcastle.why: left-handed, straight mile, all-weather, uphill finish

Nottingham.why: flat left-handed oval with a straight 6f

Pontefract.why: left-handed, undulating, the last 6f essentially uphill

Redcar.why: long flat left-handed oval with a straight mile

Ripon.why: right-handed oval, cramped bends, a 6f straight

Sandown.why: right-handed, uphill finish (own build in progress)

Southwell.why: small left-handed all-weather oval with a 5f straight

Thirsk.why: sharp left-handed oval with a 6f straight
